examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Identify entities as independently described object sets and relationships as associations between them. A weak entity needs its owner's key plus a partial key and participates totally in its identifying relationship. Cardinality and participation are separate constraints; a 1:N relationship need not imply every entity participates.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A weak entity's partial key has 2 attributes and its owner's primary key has 3 distinct attributes. How many attributes form the combined identifying key?

**Answer: 5.** The weak entity is identified within one owner by its partial key. Combining three owner-key attributes with two distinct partial-key attributes gives five key attributes.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An owner may exist without weak entities, even though each weak entity requires an owner. A relationship diamond cannot substitute for a missing entity rectangle.

Cardinality and total participation impose different constraints.
